title: Tee Higgins Questionable with Groin/Neck Injury for Steelers vs. Dolphins – NBC Sports Update
body:
Cincinnati’s receiving corps could be missing one of its most dynamic playmakers on Sunday night as wideout Tee Higgins was listed as questionable heading into the Week 5 showdown with the Miami Dolphins. Head coach Zac Taylor confirmed the report, noting that Higgins is dealing with lingering discomfort in both his groin and neck after a hard-fought victory over the New York Jets last week. The uncertainty surrounding his status adds another layer of intrigue to a matchup that already features two high‑octane offenses and could force the Bengals to reshuffle their game plan at a critical point in the season.

Higgins, who finished his rookie campaign with 57 receptions for 846 yards and seven touchdowns, has quickly become a go‑to option for quarterback Joe Burrow. His blend of size, speed and route‑running precision makes him a constant threat, especially in the red zone. If the injury sidelines him, the Bengals will likely lean more heavily on the veteran duo of Ja’Marr Chase and Tyler Boyd, while also giving more snaps to emerging talent such as rookie Jordan Miller. However, the loss of Higgins’ deep‑ball capability could limit Cincinnati’s ability to stretch Miami’s secondary, which has been aggressive in pressuring Burrow and disrupting timing routes.

The nature of Higgins’ injuries raises questions about his availability. The groin strain, a common ailment for players who make frequent cuts and accelerate into routes, can linger if not given adequate rest. Meanwhile, the neck discomfort—reported as a sore neck rather than a more serious cervical issue—may have resulted from a hard collision during the Jets game, where Higgins took several hits while battling for contested catches. Medical staff have reportedly placed him in a “questionable” category, meaning he will be evaluated up until the final moments before kickoff. In recent weeks, the Bengals have been cautious with injuries, opting to sideline players like defensive end Sam Hubbard for short periods to avoid aggravating lingering issues.

Miami, meanwhile, will likely view the potential absence of Higgins as an opportunity to press its advantage. The Dolphins’ defense has improved its pass rush under coordinator Vic Fangio, tallying 3.5 sacks per game and forcing several three‑and‑out drives. Without Higgins to draw double‑coverage, Burrow could find more one‑on‑one matchups with Chase, but the Dolphins may also double‑team the remaining top receiver, forcing Burrow to rely on shorter, quicker passes that could play into Miami’s defensive scheme. Additionally, the Dolphins’ offense, spearheaded by quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, has been efficient in the red zone, making every possession crucial in a game that could hinge on a few pivotal plays.

The broader implications for the Bengals’ playoff push are significant. At 2‑2, Cincinnati sits near the top of the AFC North but cannot afford a slip‑up against a Dolphins team that is fighting for a wild‑card spot. A win would keep the Bengals within striking distance of the division lead, while a loss could see them fall behind early in the conference race. Moreover, Higgins’ health will be a barometer for the team’s depth; if he can contribute even in a limited capacity, it would signal that the Bengals are managing injuries without sacrificing offensive potency. Conversely, a prolonged absence could expose a lack of depth at the receiver position, an issue that has haunted the team in past seasons when key playmakers have gone down.

Looking ahead, the Bengals’ medical staff will have a decisive role in the final decision. If Higgins is cleared, he will likely be eased back into the rotation, perhaps with a reduced snap count to protect his groin and neck. Should he sit out, the onus will fall on Burrow to distribute the ball more evenly and on the coaching staff to devise creative schemes that mitigate the loss. As the AFC North tightens and the race for postseason berths intensifies, every injury report becomes a strategic puzzle. Cincinnati’s ability to adapt to Higgins’ status will not only shape the outcome of the Dolphins game but could also set the tone for the remainder of the season.
